dashboard-contents.statement: The Endpoint Credential Exposure dashboard filters scans by date and shows endpoints assessed, identities with exposure, the top 5 exposed credentials and the top 10 identities.

quotes: Filter scan results by dates.
View the total number of endpoints assessed in your system.
View the total number of identities containing credential exposure issues.
View the top 5 exposed credentials found on the endpoints.
View the top 10 identities that have credential exposure issues.

scan-data-download.statement: Downloading the endpoint credential exposure scan data returns a .zip file of CSV files, one set per exposure type listing endpoints and exposed credential details.

quotes: A .zip file containing multiple CSV files is downloaded to your system.
The CSV files for each exposure type contain the list of endpoints and the exposed credential details.

risk-types-chart.statement: The dashboard donut chart groups exposed credentials by risk type, for example Browser Credentials, Windows Credentials and Privilege Escalation.

quotes: View all exposed credentials categorized by risk type (e.g., Browser Credentials, Windows Credentials, Privilege Escalation, etc.) in a donut chart, represented as percentages.

roadmap.statement: The endpoint Risk Reduction Roadmap uses a severity slider, an As of Date calendar selects the scan date, and its affected objects are identities with exposed endpoint credentials.

quotes: The interactive slider in the Risk Reduction Roadmap on the Endpoint Credential Exposure dashboard allows you to view the current risk severity of your endpoints and set a target severity level.
Select a date from the As of Date calendar to view the total number of exposed credential issues on that scan date.
Each identified risk shows the total number of affected objects (identities with exposed endpoint credentials)

cleanup-supported-types.statement: Cleanup Credentials is supported for eight exposure types: Cached Domain Logon Credentials, AWS Credentials, Saved VNC Passwords, Saved Windows Credentials, Admin AutoLogon Settings, Database Connections, Azure Credentials and Google Cloud Credentials.

quotes: For each exposure type, the table also indicates if the Cleanup Credentials feature is supported or not.
| Exposure or Scan Type | Description | Cleanup Credential |
| Cached Domain Logon Credentials | Analyzes cached domain credentials to find administrative sessions | Supported |
| AWS Credentials | Analyzes permanent AWS API keys stored in the default location | Supported |
| Saved VNC Passwords | Analyzes saved VNC connection strings across commonly used VNC applications (e.g., TigerVNC) | Supported |
| Saved Windows Credentials | Analyzes the different types of credentials stored in the Windows Credential Manager | Supported |
| Admin AutoLogon Settings | Analyzes AutoLogon registry settings that allow an administrative account to log in automatically | Supported |
| Database Connections | Analyzes saved database connection strings across commonly used database applications (e.g., pgAdmin) | Supported |
| Azure Credentials | Analyzes different types of Azure credentials stored in the default location | Supported |
| Google Cloud Credentials | Analyzes different types of GCP credentials stored in the default location | Supported |

cleanup-unsupported-types.statement: Cleanup Credentials is not supported for fifteen exposure types, which are listed with the check each performs (for example SSH Keys, LSA Protections and WDigest Settings).

quotes: For each exposure type, the table also indicates if the Cleanup Credentials feature is supported or not.
| Exposure or Scan Type | Description | Cleanup Credential |
| Modifiable Service Binaries | Checks if service binaries are modifiable and could allow privilege escalation | Not supported |
| GPO Saved Passwords | Analyzes GPO files to look for reversibly encrypted credentials | Not supported |
| Unquoted Service Paths | Analyzes all Windows service configurations for unquoted paths that can be exploited to escalate privileges | Not supported |
| Sensitive Data Files | Checks files for exposed sensitive data | Not supported |
| Windows OOBE Priv Esc | Checks for non-administrative users having write access to the Windows' Unattended installation files | Not supported |
| Saved Browser Credentials | Analyzes URLs and credentials stored in encrypted local databases of commonly used browsers | Not supported |

| Unmanaged Local Admins | Checks if accounts are local (non-domain), part of the local administrators group, and have a security identifier (SID) ending with a number other than 500 | Not supported |
| Windows OOBE Files | Analyzes Windows' Unattended installation files for credentials and insecure ACLs | Not supported |
| Elevated MSI Install Settings | Analyzes the registry to check settings that allow installation of MSI files in the elevated context | Not supported |

| Overly Permissive Administrative Memberships | Checks the local administrator groups for membership from overly permissive identities (e.g., Everyone, Authenticated Users, Domain Users, etc.) | Not supported |
| WDigest Settings | Checks the registry for settings that allow storage of plain text passwords in a reversibly encrypted form in the LSASS | Not supported |
| Modifiable PATH Variables | Checks if the path in the users' PATH variable is writable or modifiable and could allow adversaries to run under the users' context | Not supported |

| Modifiable MSI UninstallString | Checks if the UninstallString attribute of installed applications is modifiable and could allow code execution and possible privilege escalation when the application is uninstalled | Not supported |
| SSH Keys | Analyzes private SSH keys without a passphrase on the file system | Not supported |
| LSA Protections | Checks the registry keys to confirm if Local Security Authority (LSA) protection is enabled | Not supported |

cleanup-process.statement: Selected exposed credentials are queued for cleanup; the agent fetches the updated policy by checking the queue in the ITDR Admin Portal and applies the cleanup, and the Cleanup Status column tracks the state (Can be cleaned, Failed).

quotes: When you select an exposed credential for a cleanup, it's first queued for cleanup.
The agent fetches the updated policy by checking the queue in the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal and applies the cleanup process
The Cleanup Status column tracks the state of the cleanup process.
the Cleanup Status column shows Can be cleaned
If the cleanup process has failed, the Cleanup Status column shows Failed.

all-exposures-columns.statement: The All Exposures page shows Total, Cleaned Up and Available to cleanup for each exposure type and can be filtered by scan date.

quotes: The All Exposures page lists the total number of exposed endpoint credentials for each exposure or scan type.
Total: The total number of exposed credentials.
Cleaned Up: The total number of credentials that are cleaned up.
Available to cleanup: The Cleanup Credential feature support status.
You can filter this list based on a scan date.

privilege-escalation-causes.statement: The privilege-escalation page names three credential misconfigurations that can lead to escalation: not following least privilege, user account control misconfiguration such as ConsentPromptBehaviourAdmin set to 0, and AutoLogon security misconfiguration.

quotes: Non-adherence to the principle of least privilege (e.g., domain users are made part of the local administrator’s group).
Misconfiguration in user account control settings (e.g., the ConsentPromptBehaviourAdmin value is set to 0).
Security misconfiguration in AutoLogon (e.g., default credentials for admin or auto-logon credentials for an admin).

executive-report.statement: The Endpoint Credential Exposure executive report downloads as a PDF and shows endpoints scanned, findings by severity and the top 5 priority findings.

quotes: The report is downloaded to your system in the PDF format.
Endpoints Scanned: The total number of endpoints scanned.
Findings by Severity: The count of credential exposure findings categorized by severity level (Critical, High, Medium, and Low).
Top 5 Priority Findings: Displays the top 5 credential exposure risks on the affected endpoints and their severity level.

executive-report-categories.statement: The executive report groups credentials in focus into Browser Infostealer Risk, DevOps Credential Risk, Notable Credential Risk, Privilege Escalation Risk and Other Credentials.

quotes: Browser Infostealer Risk: Displays credential risk that is stored in the browser.
DevOps Credential Risk: Displays development and operations credential risk
Notable Credential Risk: Displays the critical credential risk exposed to attackers
Privilege Escalation Risk: Displays the setting risk that could allow attackers to gain elevated system access.
Other Credentials: Displays the additional credential risk that attackers could steal or spread across the system.

detail-export-formats.statement: Exposed-credential tables can be downloaded as CSV or JSON, and a ServiceNow ticket can be created from the Detailed Findings page.

quotes: You can use the Actions menu to copy specific columns from the table and download the table as a CSV or JSON file.
Click Actions to create a ServiceNow ticket to track and assess the issue.

severity-rating-method.title: How an exposed credential gets its Critical, High, Medium or Low severity
severity-rating-method.detail: The dashboard, roadmap and executive report show findings by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low), but these articles do not state how a finding's severity is assigned.

cleanup-agent.title: Which agent applies a credential cleanup
cleanup-agent.detail: The cleanup article says the agent fetches the updated policy by checking the queue in the ITDR Admin Portal, without naming the agent; the overview's credential-scan-agent gap covers the scan itself.
